summary: Red team of the extraction of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Topological Hochschild homology and integral p-adic Hodge theory (Publ. Math. IHÉS 129 (2019) 199–310; arXiv:1802.03261v2). All three recorded artifacts were re-downloaded, and their hashes match. All 114 items were re-read against the TeX and the published pages. The item-level work is good. Every numbered statement has an item, most statements are faithful, and E1–E7 and E9–E12 are real. The weak point is route order, which neither the extraction nor the review checked. Computed from data/atlas.json stage edges plus all restructuring and packet links, six routes put inputs in stages that are not upstream of their consumers, and one of them is a cycle. There are 12 findings, 6 medium and 6 low. (1) Propositions 7.16–7.17 and Corollary 8.23 (Z_p(0), Z_p(1), K_* of quasiregular semiperfect rings) are routed to RT.6. They rest on Theorem 7.15, which route 1 sends to the henselian-pairs Part II of RefinedTraceMethods; that Part II is downstream of RT.6, so this is a cycle, and route 1's brief records the back edge. (2) The §8.2 derived de Rham–Witt package sits at DD.4 but needs CR.4's Nygaard filtration on WΩ and DD.5's site, and Theorem 8.17 (RT.6/PR.3) needs DD.4. None of these is upstream. (3) Route 13 gives PR.4 proofs that use CR.4, DD.4, Theorem 8.17/TC and AΩ, none upstream of PR.4. With the confirmed RT-AREA-ktheory-2/36 link PR.4 → RT.6, the TC parts would form a cycle. (4) BMS2's §9 comparison with AΩ is routed to RT.6, which has neither AI.0 nor AI.3/AI.4/PR.6 upstream. (5) The HKR filtration and related items go to RT.1, which has neither the cotangent complex (DD.0) nor animation (E5) upstream. (6) The THH(F_p) inputs (Bökstedt periodicity and Nikolaus–Scholze IV.4.6–IV.4.13) are owned by L.5, which is not upstream of RT.6, and item 023 names two planners. Low: seventeen unrecorded source mistakes, of which the Gysin shift in Remark 1.16, the sign in Proposition 5.6 and max/min in Corollary 7.10 are the substantive ones; items copying slips or drifting; wrong page locators; incomplete Mathlib citations (surjective_fontaineTheta needs Frobenius surjective on R/p; frobeniusEquiv, the naive cotangent complex and DividedPowers are uncited); cited inputs without items; and E8's false 'corrected in the published version'. The review changed nothing, so it introduced no error. It checked only that route stages exist, not their order, and it passed E8's known field. Disclosure: this session wrote the red teams of BMS 2018 (PR #4748), Nikolaus–Scholze 2018 (PR #4708) and Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme 2024 (PR #4730). Findings 5 and 6 rely on the Nikolaus–Scholze extraction's routes (items /127, /130–/135), which that red team did not question.
checked: Independence. PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 was written by Claude Code cc-442dc5 (issue #1458, PR #1994; provenance line of the .md). REV-PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 was written by Claude Code cc-fb70e5 (PR #2407; review.json notes and reviews/REV-PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19.md). The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the four target files, and git log shows no commit by this session on them.

Disclosure. This session wrote RT-PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 (PR #4748), RT-PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18 (PR #4708) and RT-PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 (PR #4730). No finding here repeats one of theirs. Finding 5 notes that NS18 item /127 (the HKR filtration at RT.1) has the same order problem, which the NS18 red team did not raise. Finding 6 relies on the NS18 extraction's routes of IV.4.4–IV.4.13 to L.5 and on the review of RT-AREA-ktheory-2/34. The BMS18 red team's findings concern AI/CP/CR.3–CR.4 routes of BMS 2018 and do not overlap.

Sources. arXiv:1802.03261 has two versions (v1 9 February 2018, v2 9 April 2019, 'final version'); v2 is the latest and is the recorded version. All three artifacts were re-downloaded on 30 September 2026 and match the recorded sha256: v2 PDF b2338ef1…b3594038, v2 e-print 30968bad…4b91878ac (bms2.tex, 3266 lines), published PDF from Centre Mersenne 6b43d1ff…23ff23dd. Errata: Crossref lists no update or relation for 10.1007/s10240-019-00106-9, and a web search found no erratum.

Reading. The whole TeX source was read by five parallel readers, split by section groups (§§1–3, §§4–5, §§6–7, §8, §§9–11). Each compared every item in its range for statement, hypotheses and published-page locator, checked the recorded sourceIssues in range, and listed unrecorded slips and cited inputs. I personally re-checked every finding filed here at the TeX line and on the published page (published text via pdftotext; pp. 268, 270, 285 and 300 rendered as images). That includes the n = 1 computation for Remark 1.16, the Ext computation for Proposition 5.6, the equivariance computation for Proposition 11.3 and the renormalization in Propositions 6.2–6.3.

Coverage. Every numbered statement of §§1–11 has an item, as the review said. The only uncovered numbered objects are Remarks 1.13, 1.16 and 1.18 (expectations and commentary). The brief's topics were all checked: quasisyntomic rings and site (005, 028–037), flat descent for HH/THH/TC^-/TP (025–027), the Nygaard filtration (056, 058, 059, 071–076, 097), Δ̂ and A_inf/BK cohomology via TC^-/TP (004, 008, 047, 049, 106–114), motivic filtrations (009–012, 057, 061), TC^- of qrsp (055–056, 084), Bökstedt (023), Hesselholt's comparison (054), Z_p(i) (012–014, 064–070, 088), the Segal conjecture (086, 099), derived de Rham/crystalline comparisons (043, 045, 080–084), BK twists (010, 049–050) and Theorem 1.2 (002, 111–114).

Source issues. E1–E12 were re-checked at their locators in both texts. All are real, and E10 and E11 are phrased per the published text. E8's 'corrected in the published version' is false (finding 12). Seventeen further mistakes were found (finding 7). A possible gap was noted but not filed: the 'classical' surjectivity of B^× ⊗ B^× → K_2(B) for every local ring B in the proof of Proposition 7.17 is, to my knowledge, known only for residue fields with enough elements (otherwise one needs Dennis–Stein symbols). I could not settle whether this affects the w-local rings used there.

Statuses and library. The declaration index at the pin (declarations.tsv, Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474) was searched for perfectoid, tilt, Fontaine θ, Witt-vector Frobenius, cotangent complex, H1Cotangent, Kähler differentials, divided powers, Hochschild, THH, cyclotomic, de Rham–Witt, Nygaard, syntomic, crystalline, Breuil–Kisin, K-theory/Steinberg and décalage. Files read at the pin: FontaineTheta.lean (lines 30–200), Perfection.lean (PreTilt, 513–650), WittVector/Defs.lean:52, WittVector/Frobenius.lean:280–290, Extension/Cotangent/Basic.lean:61 and :552, DividedPowers/Basic.lean:70–80, DividedPowers/Padic.lean, DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean:95–102. Tau Ceti has nothing in this area (its DividedPowers files concern Kostant forms). No item marked missing is in either library.

Atlas stages read in full (data/atlas.json): RefinedTraceMethods RT.1, RT.2, RT.3, RT.3b, RT.5, RT.6; DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0–DD.5; AInfCohomology AI.0, AI.1, AI.7; CrystallineCohomology CR.0, CR.4; PrismaticCohomology PR.0, PR.2–PR.7; FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4; KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2:low-degree-comparisons; PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra; EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation. Each planned item was compared with the stage text. Only item 001's generality fails (finding 8).

Route order. The ancestor sets of all 24 cited stages were computed from data/atlas.json stageEdges and stage requirements plus every link in research/blueprint/restructure/RS-*.result.json and research/blueprint/packets/*.json (node ids mapped to their parent stages). Including unaccepted restructuring links can only add ancestors, so 'not upstream' claims are conservative. Every link proposed in the fixes was checked acyclic, both alone and together with RT-AREA-ktheory-2/36's PR.4 → RT.6.

Other extractions and red teams. PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21 and PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21 (the henselian-pairs Part II and its prerequisite), PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (route 4 and items 70, 70b, 76, 92, 95, 115), PAPER-ANTIEAU-MATHEW-MORROW-ETAL-22 (relative THH over S[z], syntomic items; review 'revise', so leads only), PAPER-LIU-WANG-22 (cyclotomic structure on THH(−/S[z]) routed to RT.2; review 'revise'), PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-23 (Avramov at DD.0, consistent with item 030) and PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18 (HKR /127, Bökstedt /130, F_p computations /131–/135, Segal Part II). Duplication in routing to the same owner (Avramov at DD.0; relative THH at RefinedTraceMethods) is consistent and is not reported. LMMT24 has no overlap with BMS2. Red teams already on main that touch these stages were read so as not to repeat them: RT-AREA-ktheory-1/2 (/34 rejected, /35 and /36 confirmed) and RT-AREA-padic-2 (/16, /28).

Review. REV-PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 changed nothing, so it introduced no error. Its checks were re-done: 173 numbered objects, range expansion of locators, library citations and stage existence. It did not check route order, and it passed E8's known field.

findings.claim: Three items routed to RT.6 are proved from Theorem 7.15 (item 063, K(S; Z_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}TC(S; Z_p) for S henselian along p with S/p semiperfect), which route 1 sends to the proposed Part II RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs. A Part II has its parent as first prerequisite (PROTOCOL §15), and the accepted Clausen–Mathew–Morrow brief makes RefinedTraceMethods its first prerequisite. So RT.6 would need a statement owned downstream of itself: a cycle. The items are Proposition 7.16 (item 065: Z_p(0) = Z_p, whose last step is 'This implies the identification Z_p(0) = lim Z/p^r by passage to the p-completion, using Theorem 7.15'), Proposition 7.17 (item 066: Z_p(1) = T_pG_m, via K_1 and K_2 of w-local rings) and Corollary 8.23 (item 089: K_*(S; Z_p) of quasiregular semiperfect S). Route 1's own brief records the back edge: Theorem 7.15 'is the bridge by which BMS2 identifies Z_p(0) = Z_p, Z_p(1) = T_pG_m and K_*(S; Z_p) = ⊕ A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i} … (routed to RefinedTraceMethods RT.6)'. Item 066 also uses item 067 (K_0, K_1, K_2 of local rings), planned at K.2:low-degree-comparisons, which is not upstream of RT.6 either. The accepted Bhatt–Scholze extraction does this correctly: its route 4 puts the K-theoretic consequences (Corollaries 14.2–14.3) in the same Part II and says 'Import PR.4 and RT.6; neither depends on this Part II'. The first of the two proofs of Proposition 7.21 (item 069, routed to PR.4) also goes through Theorem 7.15; the second, direct proof (Lemma 7.22) does not.

findings.claim: The paper has at least seventeen mistakes that the extraction and the review did not record. Each is in arXiv v2 and in the published text. (1) Remark 1.16 (p. 209): the expected triangle 'Z_p(n−1)(k) = WΩ^{n−1}_{k,log}[−n+1] → Z_p(n)(O_K) → τ^{≤n}RΓ_ét(Spec K, Z_p(n))' is missing the Gysin shift; the first term should be Z_p(n−1)(k)[−2] = WΩ^{n−1}_{k,log}[−n−1]. For n = 1 with k algebraically closed, Z_p(1)(O_K) = (O_K^×)^∧[−1] and τ^{≤1}RΓ_ét(K, Z_p(1)) = (K^×)^∧[−1]. The valuation sequence then gives the fibre Z_p[−2], not Z_p = Z_p(0)(k). Schneider's triangle has i_*ν^{n−1}[−n−1]. The Hesselholt–Madsen graded pieces in the same remark also lack [2n]. (2) Proposition 5.6 (p. 237): 'identifies with Ext^{i−c}_R(M, N) if c ≤ 0' should be Ext^{i+c}. The proof ends with RHom_R(M, N)[c], and for c = −1 the extensions [M → N] give Hom = Ext^0 in Ext^1_{Ch}. The matching slip is in the proof of Theorem 5.4 (p. 236): Ext^{a−i+j} should be Ext^{a+i−j}. The two cancel, so the theorem is unaffected. (3) §5.1 (p. 233): 'gr^i(F) = F(i)/F(i−1)' should be F(i)/F(i+1); the filtration is descending. (4) Proof of Corollary 5.10 (p. 239): '(3) The functor F ↦ F(∞)' should be F(−∞), as the next paragraph proves. (5) Proof of Lemma 4.7(2) (p. 222): 'for i < 0 is pro-zero' should be i > 0 (or i ≠ 0). (6) Proof of Propositions 6.2–6.3 (p. 246): 'Replacing ξ by φ^{−1}(α)ξ' should be φ^{−1}(α)^{−1}ξ. With u′ = cu, ξ′ = cξ and σ fixed by can(u′) = ξ′σ, φ(u′) = φ(c)ασ, so one needs φ(c) = α^{−1}. (7) Same proof (p. 247): 'assume that M is bounded below, so after shifting coconnective … assume that M is bounded above as well' has 'below' and 'above' swapped, since lim τ_{≤n}M gives bounded above, i.e. coconnective. (8) Corollary 7.10(1) (p. 258): '𝒩^iΔ̂_A ∈ D^{[0,max(i,d)]}' should be min(i, d). The graded pieces are Ω^j[−j] for 0 ≤ j ≤ i, and these vanish for j > d. With max the stated consequence (Δ̂_A, 𝒩^{≥•}) ∈ DF^{≤0}, which needs gr^i ∈ D^{≤i}, does not follow. (9) Proof of Proposition 7.17 (p. 262): 'S^{1/p} = S[X_u]/(X_u − u^p)' adjoins nothing; it should be (X_u^p − u). This is two lines before E6. (10) §7.4 (p. 261): 'As in the statement of Theorem 1.12(4)' should be 1.12(5), where Z_p(n) := gr^nTC[−2n] is defined. This is the same sentence as E5. (11) Proof of Proposition 8.5 (p. 268): the subcomplex '… → p^iFWΩ^i_A → p^{i+1}FWΩ^i_A → ⋯' should have p^{i+1}FWΩ^{i+1}_A, since φ = p^nF in degree n. (12) Proof of Proposition 8.7 (p. 270): 'H^j = pWΩ^i_A/(pVWΩ^i_A + pdVΩ^{i−1}_A) for j < i' should be pWΩ^j_A/(pVWΩ^j_A + pdVWΩ^{j−1}_A); the j = i line also needs dVWΩ^{i−1}. (13) Proposition 8.13(3) (p. 274): 'φ_i mod p : 𝒩^{≥i}LWΩ_S ≅ Lτ^{≤i}Ω_{S/F_p}' should have the graded piece 𝒩^i. By fibre sequence (4), 𝒩^i, not 𝒩^{≥i}, is Lτ^{≤i}Ω, as in Theorem 8.14(2). (14) Remark 9.11 (p. 290): 'Here, q = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf' should be q = [ε]. BMS1's q-de Rham complex has q − 1 = μ = [ε] − 1 (Notation 9.1), and only then does φ(q − 1)/(q − 1) = ξ̃ give the factor φ(d_q log T) = ξ̃ d_q log T used in §10. (15) Proposition 11.3 (p. 300): the Frobenius of B^cyN is 'given by (s, n) ↦ (s^p, pn)'. With the stated action t·(s, n) = (t^n s, n) this map is not T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant, and (s, n) ↦ (s, pn) is. Take τ = t^p acting on the C_p-fixed target; then τ·(s, pn) = (τ^n s, pn), whereas (s, n) ↦ (s^p, pn) sends (τ^n s, n) to (τ^{pn}s^p, pn) ≠ (τ^n s^p, pn). In loop terms, precomposing the loop t ↦ st^n with t ↦ t^p gives t ↦ st^{pn}. The diagram that follows only uses the n-coordinate, so nothing else changes. (16) Construction 9.13 (p. 291): THH(A; Z_p) as the p-completion of 'A ⊗_{E_∞-k} T^∧_p' should be ⊗_{E_∞-𝕊}, as in §11 ('A ⊗_{E_∞-𝕊[z]} T'); no ring k is in scope. (17) Proof of Lemma 11.6 (p. 301): the squares 𝕊[z] → O_K → A over 𝕊 → k → A ⊗_{O_K} k 'are Cartesian in E_∞-rings' should say coCartesian (pushouts); base change for THH needs pushouts, and k = O_K ⊗_{𝕊[z]} 𝕊.

findings.claim: The library citations are incomplete or inexact. (a) Item 033 states 'For a p-adically complete ring R … Fontaine's surjection θ : A_inf(R) → R', and its note says θ is 'surjective by fontaineTheta_surjective'. There is no such declaration. The theorem is surjective_fontaineTheta, and it needs the hypothesis that Frobenius is surjective on R/p. Without that hypothesis θ need not be surjective: for R = Z_p⟨T⟩, R^♭ = F_p, and θ is Z_p → Z_p⟨T⟩. (b) The Frobenius automorphism φ of A_inf(R) is WittVector.frobeniusEquiv, which applies because PreTilt is a perfect ring; item 033 does not cite it. (c) The baseline note says that neither library defines 'the cotangent complex'. Mathlib does have the naive (two-term) cotangent complex, Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex, and its H_1, Algebra.H1Cotangent. For a quotient S = R/I this H_1 is I/I² = π_1L_{S/R}, the module M that items 035, 044 and 055 use. (d) A_crys, divided power envelopes and their conjugate filtration (items 078–079) are built on divided powers. Mathlib has DividedPowers, the divided powers on (p) ⊂ Z_p, and DividedPowerAlgebra (Γ). None of these is cited, although Γ^* appears in items 044, 055 and 079.
